title: sjpw-cruiserweight
label: Super Tengu

won.source: Defeated Shinji "Live" Hamada in a pre-arranged finish at Battlecade '97, the fed's first pay-per-view, per the operator's own retrospective disclosure (promotions/sjpw/archive/too-real-jul1997.html) and his 8 June 1997 reference to Tengu as "the newly crowned SJPW Cruiserweight champion" (promotions/sjpw/archive/announcement-new-fed-8jun1997.html).

how: Lost to Ace Killcannon at the Super J Crown Tournament pay-per-view.
note: Battlecade '97 itself (7 June 1997) is not served -- a zero-body collection gap -- so `event` is left unset rather than pointed at a document that only reports the result after the fact; see the two cited sources above.

title: sjpw-cruiserweight
label: Ace Killcannon

won.source: Defeated Super Tengu at the Super J Crown Tournament pay-per-view, per the operator's own year-end review (promotions/sjpw/archive/year-end-review-dec1997.html: "his loss to Ace Kilcannon at The Super J Crown tournament"; "SJPW cruiserweight champion Ace Kilcannon").

how: Still champion as of the surviving record's end (16-18 December 1997), with Derek Mota lined up for a cage-match challenge.
note: The Super J Crown Tournament pay-per-view itself is not served -- a zero-body collection gap -- so `event` is left unset rather than pointed at the retrospective document alone.

title: sjpw-ncwf-cruiserweight
label: Masashi "Lightning" Lanther

won.source: The Okinawa Fight Club Kamikaze house show (15 May 2004) describes him as having 'held the NCWF title for a very long time' before seconding a later challenger for it.

note: The title passed to a later champion before this pass's own reading window; no document records the change, so no lost date or end_how is given.

title: sjpw-ncwf-cruiserweight
label: Super Bakemono

won.source: Billed as the reigning champion on both the Okazaki City Gym house show (10 May 2004, declining to defend) and the Okinawa Fight Club Kamikaze house show (15 May 2004, defending).

note: Successfully defended the title against El Santa Azteca in Okinawa on 15 May 2004. Lost the title before 11 August 2004; no document read to date records the change itself, gap-registered rather than invented.

lost.source: No document this pass could read records the title change; Super Bakemono is last billed as NCWF champion in the wing's own prior pass (wave C03-STRUCTURE-13, Okinawa Fight Club Kamikaze, 15 May 2004), and Masashi Lanther is first billed as champion again in this pass's own promotions/sjpw/archive/chiimu-tora-dojo-2004-08-11.html (11 August 2004). The revival's own press conference (served by wave C03-STRUCTURE-17) advance-announced a Lanther/Bakemono NCWF title match at Zenmen Sensou (26 June 2004), which this pass treats as the probable but unattested occasion for the change, consistent with that title match being unreadable under the no-network rule.

title: sjpw-grand-prix-heritage
label: Kentaro "H-Bomb" Kawasaki

won.source: First billed as GPH Champion in promotions/sjpw/archive/tokyo-club-atom-2004-07-11.html and the News & Notes bulletin of 9 July 2004, immediately after the revival's own unread Zenmen Sensou supershow (26 June 2004), where a press conference had advance-announced a new Grand Prix Heritage title; the title match itself is not attested by any document this pass could read.

note: Defended to a thirty-minute time-limit draw against Noboru "Raging Bull" Nishida (promotions/sjpw/archive/tokyo-oi-store-2004-07-19.html, 19 July 2004); billed as still champion through promotions/sjpw/archive/gyoda-citizen-gymnasium-2004-08-20.html and the News & Notes bulletin of 1 September 2004, which names Tasogare no Prince as the presumptive next challenger. Two further defenses (against Masashi Lanther on the collect-only The Zone! 8/7/04, and in a scramble trios match on the collect-only The Zone! 8/27/04) are referenced only in prose and are not structured, since neither television broadcast is fetchable under the no-network rule.

title: sjpw-ncwf-cruiserweight
label: Masashi "Lightning" Lanther

won.source: First billed as champion in promotions/sjpw/archive/chiimu-tora-dojo-2004-08-11.html (11 August 2004), defending against Shoji Suzuki to a draw; the revival's own press conference (served by wave C03-STRUCTURE-17) had advance-announced a Lanther/Bakemono title match at the unread Zenmen Sensou supershow (26 June 2004), which this pass treats as the probable, but unattested, title change.

note: Billed as champion again in promotions/sjpw/archive/tokyo-marine-2004-08-25.html (25 August 2004) and the News & Notes bulletin of 1 September 2004, which names him defending at the coming Jisedei: Tsunami supershow.
